summary.headline: Anupam Rasayan Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR655 crore (TI +36% YoY), EBITDA INR175 crore at 26% margin, PAT up only 6% to INR51 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 36% YoY to INR667.5 crore, with EBITDA up 35% to INR174.9 crore and margin steady at about 26%. PAT grew 6% to INR51.2 crore as higher depreciation (partly Jayhawk's older depreciation policy) and interest absorbed the EBITDA gain. Management said the major capex cycle is complete and Jayhawk contributed roughly 20-22% of revenue at a 19-20% EBITDA margin. The Bliss GVS Pharma open offer closed on August 10, with completion expected by the first half of September 2026.

segments.name: Jayhawk Fine Chemicals (US)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 20-22% of Q1 revenue (around INR145 crore), with EBITDA margin of 19-20% (around INR30 crore) and PAT of about INR9 crore after heavy depreciation. Management said Jayhawk is unlevered and well capitalised.

segments.name: Standalone performance materials / polymers
segments.commentary: Standalone polymer share guided at 20-25%, and 30-35% on a consolidated basis. Agro contribution was lower this quarter due to seasonal demand. Standalone gross margin was about 58%, driven mainly by performance materials.

segments.name: Agro
segments.commentary: Management said demand recovery is visible in existing agro products and that agro should be stable, with its share declining as other segments grow faster.

guidance_outlook: Organic revenue growth guided at about 25% plus or minus a few points for FY27, with Jayhawk adding another 10-15% inorganically.
Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 24-26%; consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.
Interest cost expected to stay at the current run rate; no major further capitalisation expected, so depreciation should not rise sharply from new capex.
Standalone capex guided at INR70-80 crore for now (repair, maintenance and repurposing).

Bliss GVS Pharma completion expected in the first half of September 2026, with integration to start after completion. Management targets 60-70% utilisation at Bliss over 2-3 years, versus about 30% currently.
Working capital expected to be stable and then improve, reaching the guided range by year-end FY27.
capex_capacity: Major capex cycle complete; all major planned projects commissioned and operational. Incremental capex to be selective and based on customer visibility.
Standalone capex guided at INR70-80 crore for now, mainly maintenance and repurposing.
ETFA commercialised via flow chemistry, claimed as a first globally; management says it is the only player doing this in flow.
Bliss utilisation about 30% today, targeted at 60-70% over 2-3 years. Bliss has a pipeline of 62 molecules over 2 years, including 48+ aimed at regulated markets (per the CEO's opening remarks).
demand_pricing: ETFA addressable market estimated at about USD0.5 billion across the two molecules; management said initial share of 5-10% and possibly up to 15-30%, without a firm number.
BASQUEVOLT LoI covers a potential long-term supply opportunity of about USD300 million over 10 years, with commercialisation expected in H2 FY27 and meaningful revenue in 2-3 years.
Cumulative signed LOIs and contracts represent roughly INR18,000 crore of potential business over their tenures.
Management expects order-book-linked revenue to be about 25% of revenue this year and about 30% going forward.
Semiconductor revenue is growing fast per management, with Jayhawk's semicon and defence products cited as a contributor. No quantified figures were given.
Bain & Co is supporting the PMO and IMO for Jayhawk-Anupam synergies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the API plant acquisition flagged in the last call?
qa_highlights.answer: Still exploratory with nothing to share. Management will work with Bliss management on any acquisitions once Bliss completes.

qa_highlights.question: Bliss completion timeline and pending approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: SEBI approval received and open offer closed on August 10. Procedural steps remain; completion expected by the first half of September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Jayhawk contribution and margin this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20-22% of revenue (around INR145 crore), with EBITDA margin of 19-20% (around INR30 crore) and PAT of about INR9 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will Anupam fund Jayhawk capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No requirement is foreseen; Jayhawk is well capitalised and unlevered, with only limited repurposing or replacement capex.

qa_highlights.question: How is Bliss funded?
qa_highlights.answer: A fully owned subsidiary will take about INR300 crore of debt, with the balance funded through an equity-linked instrument that Anupam can buy out at any time. Management said Bliss has over INR200 crore of cash flow and no debt, so no large external capital is needed for later API acquisitions.

risks_watch: PAT growth (6%) lagged EBITDA growth (35%) because of depreciation and interest. Jayhawk's depreciation policy is under review and may change the run rate.
Q1 is seasonally weak, and organic growth ex-Jayhawk was single digit this quarter, so the 25% organic guidance needs a strong H2.
Bliss completion depends on procedural steps, and management declined to give Bliss-specific numbers or CDMO timelines before consummation.
HFC-32 quota status for Tanfac was deferred to Tanfac management; no confirmation given on Anupam's side.
Working capital was described as stable and not improving; management expects it to reach the guided range by year-end.
Open-offer acceptance was very small, so the Bliss stake cost is largely fixed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, new products and the Bliss and BASQUEVOLT opportunities. Guarded and deferential on Bliss-specific numbers, CDMO and Tanfac HFC-32 quota, citing listed-company constraints until the deal closes. Margin and capex guidance was given with clear numbers.
key_quotes: And to our knowledge, we are the only ones who are able to do it in flow today.
We expect commercialization to begin during FY27 and we'll gradually scale the opportunity based on customer requirement.
So we continue to believe that we should be able to improve the utilization of the company's assets to 60% to 70%, and that would translate to the kind of numbers that are there, that would be there.
